cases.title: Billing architecture
cases.text:
Billing architecture
Each billing change needs a migration plan that a lead reviews.
The invoice service never writes to the ledger table directly.
All money amounts are stored as integer paise, never as a float.
A refund over 50,000 rupees needs a second approver.

cases.title: Platform rules
cases.text:
Platform rules
1. Every service writes its logs as JSON lines to standard output.
2. Every public route needs a session, and no route reads a tenant from the body.
3. Each database table carries organization_id under forced row level security.
4. A migration only adds columns, and a rename waits for a later release.
5. No service holds a database session open across a model call.
6. Every new feature ships behind a flag that is off by default.
7. A secret never appears in a log line or in an error message.
8. Each money amount is an integer number of paise.
9. The gateway is the only service that faces the internet.
10. A background job binds the member who owns the work that it does.
11. Each outbound request to a member's address goes through the outbound guard.
12. A test that needs a database runs against a real Postgres server.
13. Each model call passes a feature name for the usage report.
14. Text that a stranger wrote never reaches the model outside a frame.

cases.title: Storage rules
cases.text:
Storage rules
Each upload is scanned for malware before a member can open it.
A file over 25 megabytes goes to cold storage after thirty days.
No file is shared outside the organization without a signed link.
Each deleted file stays restorable for fourteen days.
